t: Find if Digit Game Can Be Won
o:
## Understanding the problem

Alice picks ALL single-digit numbers or ALL double-digit numbers from nums; Bob gets the rest. Alice wins iff her sum is strictly greater than Bob's.

Example 1 `[1,2,3,4,10]`: singles sum 10, doubles sum 10, total 20 — neither choice gives strictly more than 10 → false. Example 2 `[1,2,3,4,5,14]`: singles 15 vs doubles 14 → true. Example 3 `[5,5,5,25]`: doubles 25 vs singles 15 → true.

There are only two choices, so compute both sums and compare each against half the total with strict inequality.
k: Alice's two options are exactly: sum of elements < 10, or sum of elements ≥ 10.
She wins iff max(singleSum, doubleSum) · 2 > totalSum (strict inequality matters — ties lose).

a.i: Partition the total into single-digit and double-digit sums in one pass; Alice wins if either bucket alone strictly exceeds the complement.
s: Accumulate s (elements < 10) and d (elements ≥ 10); total = s + d.

w:
## Wrap-up

Trivial once framed as two buckets. The strict '>' is the only trap: example 1 has both buckets equal to 10, and equality means Bob wins (or ties go to Bob per the statement). A follow-up might generalize to k digit-length buckets — same idea with k sums.
